headline: Additional $50,000 approved for cleanup of Comblok site, where 173 affordable housing units are planned.
summary: The extra money brings the city's grant to $500,000, the most EPA rules allow per site. Portland Housing's development officer said phase one cleanup should be fully complete in January of this upcoming year. The first building, with 55 family apartments, is expected to be complete in November of 2027. An additional Brownfield grant was also approved for the Roo Institute's site.
decisions: Approved an additional 50,000 Brownfield grant for the Roo Institute by roll call, 6-0.
Approved an additional $50,000 Brownfield grant for Portland Housing Authority's Comblok site.
discussion: Roo Institute grant: The presentation showed site photos and a plan to finish construction this coming year. The extra money would pay for off-site soil disposal that will be needed soon, and comments praised the project's design.
Comblok site cleanup: The presentation said city money now goes only to phase one, which frees EPA funds for phase two. Phase two has hazardous material that costs more to dispose of.
Real estate gap loan: A possible real estate loan with gap financing could need a special meeting before the third Thursday in December.

Economic development ideas: Remarks suggested partnering with the Roo Institute, Portland Downtown or the Chamber to raise the city's visibility. A new head of the economic development department is expected soon.
